nodes.label: Kedai Jaga (killed)
nodes.rationale: Stallholders noticing when a senior living alone stops coming; killed because SDP controls no daily-regular venue and paid visits (Teman, Rakan Penjaga) already exist.

nodes.label: Night-flow leak check (cut seed)
nodes.rationale: Cut in round 3 at 61: thin evidence that hidden leaks are common during the defect liability period.

nodes.label: Penjaga Taman (narrowed seed)
nodes.rationale: One paid network of retiree watchers checking empty homes and visiting parents, as Japan Post does; narrowed back to empty homes because paid senior visits already exist in Malaysia.

nodes.label: 24-month defect liability period
nodes.rationale: Standard Malaysian sale contracts give 24 months and 30 days to repair after written notice; Singapore's HDB adds 5 years for leaks and Japan 10 years for rain-keeping parts.

nodes.label: One-tap rain-stamped defect report
nodes.rationale: Owner answers dry, damp or leaking; damp or leaking files a defect with a photo stamped with rainfall, gauge and time; dry tells SDP the house passed that storm.

nodes.label: PACC (SDP performance analytics and command centre)
nodes.norm_label: pacc (sdp performance analytics and command centre)

nodes.label: RainCheck (US stormwater inspection software)
nodes.rationale: Name clash that renamed Rain-Check to Lepas Hujan; it triggers inspection deadlines from rainfall, but for contractors' stormwater compliance.

nodes.label: Trinity Group Gold Assurance Programme
nodes.rationale: Closest Malaysian offer: 36-month defect period and 10-year roof-leak warranty; the red-team answer is that a warranty only pays if someone notices the leak.

nodes.label: Selangor 2026 dengue surge
nodes.rationale: 31,782 cases by week 40 of 2026, up 72.6% on 2025, with 31 deaths against 6; Petaling district, including Elmina, up 79.2%.

nodes.label: Vacant new homes
nodes.rationale: 2020 census: 19.4% of Malaysia's living quarters vacant; in Petaling 62.9% of vacant ones were newly completed or for rent or sale. Councils won't enter abandoned private houses to clean them.

nodes.label: Lepas Hujan
nodes.rationale: Planet track, climate resilience: when heavy rain falls on a phase, the SDP App asks new owners to check for roof and window leaks, and one tap files a rain-stamped defect report while the defect liability period still covers them. Rank 1 of 8 (74.0), the only idea all three judges scored 4 on innovation, and SDP can run it alone; its climate fit is weak (fit 3 from every judge), so it falls to fifth at 50% fit.

nodes.label: Rumah Dijaga
nodes.rationale: People track, healthy lifestyles: monthly outside checks by a local retiree keep new SDP homes whose owners don't move in free of mosquito breeding, overgrowth and unnoticed defects through the defect period, sold via the SDP App. Rank 8 of 8 (52.3): no evidence the problem exists or that owners will pay; kept as a record, not a candidate.

nodes.label: Five resident persona agents
nodes.rationale: Each agent brainstormed alone from one resident's week (working parent in Elmina West, retired couple in Bandar Bukit Raja, renter and rider in Denai Alam, SDP's Elmina township manager, Serenia City engineer), because asking one model for ideas makes them alike. 40 seeds.

nodes.label: Sticky neighbourhood scheme pattern
nodes.rationale: From 30 neighbourhood schemes worldwide with published usage numbers: schemes stick when the service comes to the door on a schedule, rides a payment people already make, or gives a named neighbour a role.

nodes.label: Neighbour buddy pair (main and backup)
nodes.rationale: Buddies are chosen from neighbours on higher floors or higher ground so a buddy's own flooding doesn't break the plan; messages go through WhatsApp so nobody installs a new app.

nodes.label: Rainfall-at-leak design standard by house type
nodes.norm_label: rainfall-at-leak design standard by house type
nodes.rationale: Learning which house types leak at what rainfall lets SDP fix whole batches and feed designers of the next phase; it is the climate-resilience evidence an adaptation plan for heavier rain needs, folded in after judges called the climate label a stretch.

nodes.label: Rain-triggered leak check prompt
nodes.rationale: When 24-hour rainfall at the nearest JPS gauges passes about 40 mm, owners in that phase get one message to check ceilings, window frames and the car porch. Gauges, not models, because Open-Meteo showed under 5 mm near Elmina on days gauges recorded 47 to 48 mm.

nodes.label: Monthly outside check by a local retiree
nodes.norm_label: monthly outside check by a local retiree
nodes.rationale: About 20 minutes on a checklist adapted from Japan Post's empty-house service, outside only and with no keys; sold as maintenance, not security, to stay outside the Private Agencies Act 1971 and limit liability. The checker tips standing water, applies larvicide and files visible defects.

nodes.label: Judging matrix
nodes.rationale: Six slide-26 criteria scored 1 to 5 with anchors at 1, 3 and 5; weights Impact 25%, Innovation 20%, Feasibility 20%, Fit 15%, Commercial 10%, Evidence 10%. Innovation anchors resolve the brief's conflict: new in Malaysia scores 3, not found anywhere scores 5.

nodes.label: First ideation (10 October 2026)
nodes.rationale: Ten rounds: 33 seeds from SDP's admitted gaps, township pain points, SDP-owned assets and the 14 focus areas; gates left 14, scoring kept 10, research and red-teaming left four finalists.

nodes.label: Fit-out opt-out (minus option)
nodes.rationale: Merged into Handover Loop then dropped in round 4: South Korea's minus option had 1 taker in 507 homes in 2008, about 12% at one complex in 2016.

nodes.label: Flood car refuge (killed)
nodes.rationale: Killed in round 8: MBSA already opened Sri Muda's multi-storey car park during floods in 2022, and no SDP mall or multi-storey car park was found in Bandar Bukit Raja.

nodes.label: Independent AI judge panel
nodes.rationale: Three judge agents play SDP's head of sustainability, an SDP township general manager and an external innovation mentor; they score against the judging matrix without seeing the author's scores, and the ranking rule (judges' mean) is set before they report.

nodes.label: Second ideation (16 October 2026)
nodes.rationale: Started because the first finalists all scored 3 or less on innovation and none had weekly use; 77 seeds from X posts, five persona agents, own lenses and a neighbourhood-scheme scan, filtered by two new gates.

nodes.label: Sedia Asing (killed)
nodes.rationale: Recycling defaults set at key handover; killed because Selangor's SELKitar already gives bins and door-to-door collection, and KDEBWM and councils choose the areas.

nodes.label: Bandar Bukit Raja recurring floods
nodes.rationale: November 2024 flash flood reached 2,000 homes across 10 neighbourhoods; further floods on 16 February, 20 April and 8 May 2026; warnings came hours late.

nodes.label: Japan's individual evacuation plans (Disaster Countermeasures Basic Act)
nodes.norm_label: japan's individual evacuation plans (disaster countermeasures basic act)
nodes.rationale: Closest analogue: lists mandatory since 2013, individual plans since 2021, but in 52.8% of municipalities 20% or fewer of listed people had a plan, which sets the coverage bar.

nodes.label: Silent-pair escalation ladder
nodes.rationale: A pair silent for 30 minutes passes to the backup buddy, then the residents' association coordinator, then the civil defence force (APM).

nodes.label: Ormond Beach continuous monitoring and adaptive control
nodes.norm_label: ormond beach continuous monitoring and adaptive control

nodes.label: Bandar Bukit Raja Wetland Townpark
nodes.rationale: SDP says it can retain over 50,000 m³ (SR2025 p. 58); a 2026 StarPicks feature says it and the 2027 Wetland Nature Park will hold 150,000 m³ together, a conflict flagged in the doc.

nodes.label: QR-tagged sapling adoption
nodes.rationale: Nearby residents adopt saplings and get watering prompts in dry spells, because stewardship drives survival (99.4% annual survival in one US programme vs 44% five-year mortality across Asian restoration sites). No judge thought adopters would keep watering without rewards.

nodes.label: SDP 250,000-tree target
nodes.rationale: 191,827 planted by 2025 against 250,000 by 2030; the report gives no survival, canopy or shade figure, so the target counts planting, not benefit.

nodes.label: Sorted weighed drop point
nodes.rationale: A 12-month sorted drop point on a vacant lot, each load weighed and logged to the unit, priced below MBSA's RM290 debris bin; runs on price and convenience because nothing compels contractors after handover.

nodes.label: Gates
nodes.rationale: Pass/fail filters from the brief's rules and CONTEXT takeaways (not taken, not a re-skin, within SDP's reach, no unrouted blocker, buildable, specific, real use, beyond the first ideation); an idea failing a gate is cut whatever its score.

nodes.label: Idea ranking
nodes.rationale: Evidence for the team's pick in issue #18, not the pick itself; ranks eight ideas from two ten-round AI ideations by the second panel's mean judge score. No human has scored the ideas and no resident has been interviewed, so a gap of a few points is a tie.

nodes.label: Recommendation
nodes.rationale: Pick Lepas Hujan or Kolam Sedia, tied 1.3 points apart and both Planet climate resilience. Settle by Sun 18 Oct: Lepas Hujan passes if 3 of 10 Elmina owners found leaks only in heavy rain or too late; Kolam Sedia passes if SDP confirms gated or pumped outlets. Default to Lepas Hujan because it needs no outside party. Pitch one idea; drop Rumah Dijaga and Handover Loop.

nodes.label: Jiran Siaga
nodes.rationale: People track, safety: gives residents of Bandar Bukit Raja's flood-prone streets who can't evacuate alone two neighbour buddies, a written plan and a gauge trigger. Rank 4 of 8 (68.0), rank 1 in the first panel; highest impact as a risk to life, but trigger and liability are its risks. The residents' association holds the register and SDP only convenes, to limit liability.

nodes.label: Kolam Sedia
nodes.rationale: Planet track, climate resilience: cheap water-level sensors catch blocked outlets in SDP's Bandar Bukit Raja flood ponds and a tide-aware rule sets seasonal levels. Rank 2 of 8 (72.7), first of eight at 50% fit; two of three judges ranked it first because SDP can approve the core alone on ponds it owns. It closes two gaps SDP admits: static flood maps and maintenance.

nodes.label: Teduh
nodes.rationale: Planet track: sites SDP's remaining trees where City of Elmina residents walk and wait in the sun, and keeps them alive; the headline is shade-hours to people on foot, not trees planted. Rank 5 of 8 (66.7): cheapest to build and prove, but small, slow impact and 0/3 repeat use.

nodes.label: Handover Loop
nodes.rationale: Planet track, waste: helps new Elmina homeowners and renovators dispose of renovation debris legally, cheaply and sorted in the first year after handover, when debris is heaviest and dumping easiest. Rank 7 of 8 (62.0): no lever after handover, recommended to drop.

nodes.label: Beyond the first ideation gate
nodes.rationale: Added in the second ideation so it would not return variants of first-ideation finalists or cut seeds; kids' safe walking routes, flood-depth posts and drill maps were cut by it.

nodes.label: 50% strategic fit stress test
nodes.rationale: The briefing put strategic fit at 50% (Dina, 37:04) against 15% on slide 26. Re-weighting flips the top two: Kolam Sedia leads at 81.2 and Lepas Hujan falls to fifth because every judge scored its fit 3; hence the Telegram question.

nodes.label: Real use gate
nodes.rationale: Added in the second ideation because no first-ideation finalist was something residents would use every week. An idea must name its moment of use, frequency and a non-prize hook (own money, time, safety or an existing obligation); anything used less than once a year needs a money hook.

nodes.label: Repeat-use test
nodes.rationale: Each judge said whether the named user would use the idea repeatedly without prizes. It split the eight in half: yes for the four tied to a person's own money, safety or a deadline; no for the four relying on prizes, volunteers or paying before anything goes wrong.

nodes.label: Four-signal local flood trigger
nodes.rationale: No JPS gauge sits on Sungai Puloh (nearest gauges 4.7 and 5.1 km away), so the trigger combines MET Malaysia thunderstorm warnings, JUPEM high-tide predictions, JPS gauges and SDP pond sensors; two-stage Get ready / Go alerts limit alert fatigue.

nodes.label: Drain-down outlet fault diagnosis
nodes.rationale: Comparing each pond's post-rain recession with its own record flags silt, blocked outlets or stuck flap gates; outlet faults caught before a storm are counted directly, so the pilot proves something even in a dry season. Judges' critique made this the headline outcome.

nodes.label: Tide-aware seasonal pond levels
nodes.rationale: Storm-by-storm drawdown fails because Klang's thunderstorm warnings come too late (8 May 2026 warning at 7.20 pm after rain from midday); instead hold gated ponds lower through the monsoon and spring-tide weeks, releasing at low tide. It needs JPS agreement, so the second panel suggested dropping it.

nodes.label: Shade-hours and survival metric
nodes.rationale: Replaces trees planted as the reported number; after judges' critique the lead evidence became measured person-minutes in midday sun at the top 10 stops, with projected shade-hours as supporting model output.

nodes.label: Shade-need ranking of walking segments and stops
nodes.norm_label: shade-need ranking of walking segments and stops
nodes.rationale: Scores every Elmina walking segment and bus stop by heat exposure (Sentinel-2, Landsat), people on foot (GTFS stops, OSM paths, schools, shops) and missing canopy (ESA WorldCover); Landsat's 100 m thermal bands are context only.

nodes.label: Compulsory debris deposit (dropped)
nodes.rationale: Dropped because Regulation 11(2) of the housing regulations bars collecting any payment beyond the sale contract; a compulsory deposit is likely unlawful.

nodes.label: Debris wave forecast from handover bookings
nodes.norm_label: debris wave forecast from handover bookings
nodes.rationale: The claimed novelty: forecast weekly debris per street from SDP's key-handover bookings. Bookings aren't public, so the prototype models them from published unit counts and labels them as modelled.

nodes.label: SDP 2025 AGM traffic answer
nodes.rationale: A shareholder wrote SDP 'seems not to care' about Elmina's traffic; SDP blamed 'a surge in external traffic' using its roads as shortcuts to GCE and DASH.

nodes.label: Tip-It Friday (merged seed)
nodes.rationale: Ovitraps counted by SDP's crews; merged into Jiran Projek because Singapore already maps high-mosquito areas from Gravitraps and trap counts give only modest early warning.

nodes.label: X resident-post research
nodes.rationale: 1,013 posts across 82 queries via the team's second X account, gaps filled by Brave's x.com index and fxtwitter; the loudest signal was City of Elmina's daily gridlock.

nodes.label: One-tap nuisance report with sensor readings
nodes.norm_label: one-tap nuisance report with sensor readings
nodes.rationale: Residents tap dust, noise, lorries or standing water and each report attaches the readings and wind direction at that minute, so the contractor can't wave it away.

nodes.label: Bangalore peak-spreading counter-evidence
nodes.rationale: A 2024 field experiment found a moderate, linear density-delay effect and limited welfare gains from peak spreading; the doc argues Elmina's single exit bottleneck differs but says the pitch must raise it first.

nodes.label: City of Elmina exit gridlock
nodes.rationale: One of Elmina's most-voiced complaints ('An 1km exit to my house takes an hour'); road fixes (GCE interchange, DASH link) are years away and there is no bus to switch to.

nodes.label: Gate-log off-peak prize draw
nodes.rationale: Weekly prize draw entries for each weekday leaving before 6:45 or after 8:30, detected by the gate log so nobody opens an app; prizes funded by Elmina Lakeside Mall tenants and SDP. A draw stretches a small budget, per Infosys's INSTANT raffle.

nodes.label: SDP goes first (own lorries off peak)
nodes.norm_label: sdp goes first (own lorries off peak)

nodes.label: Jiran Projek
nodes.rationale: People track, community wellbeing: paired boundary sensors, a one-tap report and weekly mosquito-egg counts let Elmina residents beside SDP building sites see dust, noise and breeding and get them fixed, via a monthly site grade in SDP's contractor evaluation. Rank 3 of 8 (69.3), the strongest People idea; SDP's HSSE team must agree to publish grades.

nodes.label: Waktu Lancar
nodes.rationale: People track, mobility: rewards gated-precinct households in City of Elmina for leaving outside the morning peak, detected from existing gate logs, after first measuring residents' share of the queue. Rank 6 of 8 (64.3): tackles the loudest complaint but no judge thought residents would keep shifting without prizes, so it goes only in the appendix or Q&A.

nodes.label: Boundary ovitrap egg counts
nodes.rationale: Weekly ovitrap rounds on site boundaries and unsold plots extend the pest-control work Selangor already requires; the outcome is breeding sites cleared, not cases, because a Malaysian trap trial found no case difference in its main analysis.

nodes.label: Monthly site grade in contractor evaluation
nodes.norm_label: monthly site grade in contractor evaluation
nodes.rationale: Dust hours, out-of-hours noise, reports resolved in 7 days and breeding sites cleared feed a grade residents can see; round 8 changed it to publish a grade per site before naming any contractor.

nodes.label: Paired upwind-downwind boundary sensors
nodes.rationale: Scoring downwind minus upwind PM10 and noise separates the site's dust from haze (Shah Alam AQI 172 on 16 October 2026), so absolute thresholds were abandoned in round 4 and SDP can prove when dust isn't its own.

nodes.label: Bottleneck queuing model (Small 2015)
nodes.rationale: At a bottleneck, queuing cost rises with the square of the number of drivers, so 10% fewer peak drivers cuts total congestion cost by about 19%; this is why a small shift matters at Elmina's single exit.

nodes.label: Measure-first resident share phase
nodes.rationale: Weeks 1 to 4 export access-card or RFID gate logs and TomTom speeds to learn how much of the queue is residents, which SDP doesn't know; it answers SDP's AGM claim that outsiders cause the jam, and the township manager judge would approve it today for the cost of a log export.

Ideas judges expected repeat use for without prizes (own money, safety or deadline)
Interventions that surface hidden leaks and defects inside the defect liability period
